sceneCN: 这里 interview 是「面试」（第 1 个义项：为判断是否录用而进行的问答），句意为那场面试只持续了不到二十分钟。画面里的物件：简历、录音笔、两张椅子。

pos.zh: 名词：面试；采访；面谈
动词：对……进行面试；采访

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「面试官；采访者」
由本词加 -ee 构成，义为「受面试者；受访者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「面试工作；访谈方法」

senses.title: Questions for a job
senses.definition: a formal meeting where an employer asks a candidate questions to judge their suitability
senses.definitionCN: 雇主向候选人提问以判断其是否适合的正式会面
senses.example: Her interview at the bank is on Friday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她在银行的面试定在周五上午。
senses.why: The prefix inter- means between and videre means to see, so the word first meant seeing each other face to face.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 inter- 意为「之间」，videre 意为「看见」，所以本义是「彼此见面」。

senses.title: Questions for the public
senses.definition: a conversation in which a journalist asks someone questions for print or broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 记者为报刊或广播电视向某人提问的对谈
senses.example: The singer gave a long interview about her new record.
senses.exampleCN: 这位歌手就新专辑接受了一次长采访。
senses.why: Journalism reused the face-to-face meeting and turned it into published words.
senses.whyCN: 新闻业借用这种面对面见面，把它变成发表出来的文字。

senses.title: The verb of asking
senses.definition: to ask someone questions in such a meeting, or to be asked them
senses.definitionCN: 在此类会面中向某人提问，或接受提问
senses.example: They interviewed six people for the post.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这个职位面试了六个人。
senses.why: English turned the noun into a verb without changing its shape.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个名词直接转成动词，形式不变。

senses.title: A private talk
senses.definition: a formal private meeting between parties who need to exchange views
senses.definitionCN: 需要交换看法者之间的正式私下会面
senses.example: The minister granted an interview to the delegation.
senses.exampleCN: 部长接见了代表团并与之会谈。
senses.why: The word also keeps its neutral sense of two parties meeting to talk.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也保留了「两方会面交谈」这一中性义。

intro.en: Interview joins Latin inter- "between" and videre "to see": a meeting face to face.
intro.cn: interview 把拉丁语 inter-「之间」与 videre「看见」合起来：一次面对面的会面。

items.en: Entreveue in French meant a meeting where people see each other.
items.cn: 法语的 entreveue 指彼此见面的会晤。

items.en: English borrowed interview in the sixteenth century for a formal meeting.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪借入 interview，指正式会晤。

items.en: Newspapers turned the meeting into a published question-and-answer.
items.cn: 报纸把这种会面变成刊登出来的问答。

items.en: Employers borrowed it for judging job candidates.
items.cn: 雇主借用它指对求职者的考察。

items.en: Broadcasting made the interview a household word.
items.cn: 广播电视让 interview 成为家喻户晓的词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -view root of seeing; the near-meaning group holds kinds of talk.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -view「看见」词根；近义组收各类谈话。

entries.definition: To look again at something in order to judge.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「复查；评论」。

entries.definition: What can be seen, or an opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「景色；看法」。

entries.definition: The person being asked the questions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「受访者；受面试者」。

entries.definition: An informal talk between people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「交谈」，语气随意。

entries.definition: A short test performance for a role.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「试演」，偏艺术行当。

entries.definition: A formal session where evidence is heard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「听证会」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the face-to-face picture of two people looking at each other.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「两个人面对面看着对方」的画面。

normal.en: inter- between plus view see equals seeing each other.
normal.cn: inter-「之间」加 view「看」就是彼此相见。

normal.en: A job interview is a view of you taken from across a desk.
normal.cn: 求职面试就是隔着桌子取你的一张「看法」。

normal.en: The boss interviews; the candidate is interviewed.
normal.cn: 老板面试别人，候选人被面试。

normal.en: Magazines print the interview as questions and answers.
normal.cn: 杂志把采访印成问答。

normal.en: View also lives in review and preview.
normal.cn: view 也活在 review 与 preview 里。

abstract.en: An interview is a short, formal version of being known.
abstract.cn: 面试是「被了解」这件事的简短正式版。

abstract.en: Two strangers look at each other and call it seeing.
abstract.cn: 两个陌生人互相打量，然后管这叫「看见」。

abstract.en: The room is small because the stakes are large.
abstract.cn: 房间很小，是因为赌注很大。

examples.en: He prepared for the interview by reading the company report.
examples.cn: 他为面试做了准备，读了公司的报告。

examples.en: The paper published a rare interview with the coach.
examples.cn: 报纸刊登了这位教练少有的专访。

examples.en: They will interview three more applicants tomorrow.
examples.cn: 他们明天还要面试另外三名申请者。

dict_mnemonic.text: inter（之间）+ view（看）——彼此当着面看一看

root: 拉丁语 inter「之间」+ videre「看见」→ 古法语 entreveue「会面」→ 英语 interview。同族有 interviewer、interviewee、review。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: a job interview, a media interview, the verb of asking, and a formal private meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：求职面试、媒体采访、提问这个动作，以及正式私下会晤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two chairs facing each other with nothing but a recorder between.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张面对面的椅子，中间只放一台录音机。

branches.en: THE DESK: an employer weighs a candidate.
branches.cn: 办公桌这条线：雇主掂量候选人。

branches.en: THE MICROPHONE: a journalist gathers words for print.
branches.cn: 话筒这条线：记者为刊登收集话语。

branches.en: THE QUESTION: the act of asking itself.
branches.cn: 问题这条线：提问这个动作。

branches.en: THE DOOR: a formal private meeting of two sides.
branches.cn: 门口这条线：两方的正式私下会面。

branches.en: THE LINK: both are controlled talk with a purpose.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都是有目的、被掌控的谈话。

intro.en: Interview is inter- "between" plus the Latin root vid- "see", with the French participle ending.
intro.cn: interview 是 inter-「之间」加拉丁词根 vid-「看见」，词尾来自法语分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre is recorded, and French entreveue is its medieval meeting form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 有记载，法语 entreveue 是它中世纪的会面形式。

items.example: It marks the mutual position.
items.exampleCN: 它标出相互之间的位置。

items.example: The root also appears in vision and evident.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 vision 与 evident。

items.example: The verb is the base of the root.
The French noun is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词是直接来源。

items.example: It forms interviewer.
It forms interviewee.
It forms review, to see again.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 review，意为再看一次。

items.example: It forms preview, to see beforehand.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 preview，意为预先看到。

definition_en: moving to a position inside something, changing to a new state, or showing direction of attention
core_image: 一支箭正穿过门框，箭头已经进到屋子里面
scene: 孩子端着热汤从厨房走到客厅，小心地跨过门槛。She walked into the room without knocking.
sceneCN: 这里 into 是「到……里面」（第 1 个义项：向内的移动），句意为她没敲门就走进了房间。画面里的物件：门槛、端着的汤碗、门框。

pos.zh: 介词：到……里面；进入；变成；对……

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 to 构成，义为「在……里面」
结构平行的词，义为「到……上面」
功能相近的方位介词，义为「朝向」

senses.title: Movement to the inside
senses.definition: to a position inside a place, container, or space
senses.definitionCN: 到一个地方、容器或空间的里面
senses.example: He poured the milk into a tall glass.
senses.exampleCN: 他把牛奶倒进一只高玻璃杯里。
senses.why: In names the position; to names the movement. Into fuses both in one word.
senses.whyCN: in 表示位置，to 表示移动；into 把两者合成一个词。

senses.title: A change of state
senses.definition: showing the result of a change from one state or form to another
senses.definitionCN: 表示从一种状态或形态变成另一种的结果
senses.example: The water froze into solid ice overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 水一夜之间冻成了坚冰。
senses.why: Change is pictured as entering a new container called a state.
senses.whyCN: 变化被想象成走进一个叫「状态」的新容器。

senses.title: Collision or contact
senses.definition: showing that something strikes or meets something else
senses.definitionCN: 表示某物撞到或遇到另一物
senses.example: The car ran into the fence at the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在拐角处撞上了栅栏。
senses.why: Running into a thing means moving into the space it fills.
senses.whyCN: run into 某物，就是进入它占据的那块空间。

senses.title: Interest and attention
senses.definition: showing what someone is interested in or is examining closely
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人感兴趣或正在仔细查看的对象
senses.example: She is really into old films these days.
senses.exampleCN: 她最近非常迷老电影。
senses.why: Attention is also movement: the mind goes into whatever it studies.
senses.whyCN: 注意力也是一种移动：心走进它所研究的东西。

intro.en: Into is a native English compound of in and to, first written as two words.
intro.cn: into 是英语本土词，由 in 与 to 合成，最初写作两个词。

items.en: In and to were separate words with separate jobs.
items.cn: in 与 to 是两个各司其职的独立词。

items.en: Writers placed them side by side for movement inward.
items.cn: 写作者把它们并排放在一起表示向内的移动。

items.en: The two were written as one word in the medieval period.
items.cn: 中世纪时期这两个词被写成一个词。

items.en: Into became the standard form for motion and change.
items.cn: into 成为表示移动与变化的标准形式。

items.en: Idioms such as run into and be into widened its range.
items.cn: run into 与 be into 等习语又扩大了它的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other small prepositions of place; the near-meaning group holds older motion words.
note.cn: 形近组收其他表方位的小介词；近义组收较古的移动词。

entries.definition: Position inside, not movement.
entries.definitionCN: 介词义为「在……里面」，表位置。

entries.definition: An archaic form meaning to or toward.
entries.definitionCN: 介词义为「向」，古旧用法。

entries.definition: Movement to a position on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 介词义为「到……上面」。

entries.definition: Within the limits of something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词义为「在……之内」，语气更实。

entries.definition: In the direction of, without entering.
entries.definitionCN: 介词义为「朝向」，不含进入。

entries.definition: Inside a space or a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 介词义为「在……之内」，偏书面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks treat the word as in plus to walking through a door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个词看成 in 加 to 一起穿过一道门。

normal.en: Into is simply in and to run together.
normal.cn: into 就是 in 与 to 并在一起。

normal.en: In is where you are; into is how you got there.
normal.cn: in 是你在哪，into 是你怎么进去的。

normal.en: Change also uses into: ice into water, paper into ash.
normal.cn: 变化也用 into：冰成水、纸成灰。

normal.en: Run into someone means meet them by accident.
normal.cn: run into someone 意思是偶然碰上。

normal.en: Be into a band means the band is where your mind goes.
normal.cn: be into a band 意思是心都往那支乐队里去。

abstract.en: Into is a word shaped like a doorway.
abstract.cn: into 是一个长得像门口的词。

abstract.en: Every change of state is a small migration inward.
abstract.cn: 每一次状态转变都是一次向内的迁徙。

abstract.en: We fall into habits as easily as into chairs.
abstract.cn: 我们掉进习惯，就像落进椅子那么自然。

examples.en: The cat slipped into the box and refused to come out.
examples.cn: 猫钻进箱子，怎么也不肯出来。

examples.en: The argument turned into a long silence.
examples.cn: 那场争论最后变成了长久的沉默。

examples.en: He is into repairing old bicycles.
examples.cn: 他很热衷于修旧自行车。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ to（朝）——朝着里面去

root: 古英语 in「在内」+ to「向」→ 中世纪合写为 into，表示向内的移动与状态变化。同族有 in、inside、unto。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: motion inside, change of state, collision, and direction of interest.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：向内的移动、状态变化、相撞，以及兴趣所指。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow already halfway through a doorway.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭已穿过门框一半。

branches.en: THE CUP: liquid moving to the inside of a container.
branches.cn: 杯子这条线：液体移进容器内部。

branches.en: THE ICE: one state becoming another.
branches.cn: 冰这条线：一种状态变成另一种。

branches.en: THE FENCE: a moving thing meets a solid thing.
branches.cn: 栅栏这条线：运动之物撞上实体。

branches.en: THE RECORD: attention travelling to a favourite subject.
branches.cn: 唱片这条线：注意力移向偏爱的主题。

branches.en: THE LINK: both read an abstract space as a room to enter.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都把抽象空间当成可进的房间。

intro.en: Into has no Latin pieces: it is the native in joined to to.
intro.cn: into 没有拉丁成分：它是本土的 in 接上 to。

latinIntro.en: This word is Germanic, so there are no Latin entries to list here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故此处无须列出拉丁词条。

items.example: It names the end position.
It names the direction of travel.
The compound carries both ideas at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词同时带着两个意思。

items.example: The same pattern with on instead of in.
items.exampleCN: 同一结构，把 in 换成 on。

items.example: An older form that lost ground.
It names the inner space itself.
items.exampleCN: 它指里面那块空间本身。

items.example: It keeps the direction without the entry.
The formal cousin of in.
items.exampleCN: 它是 in 的书面表亲。

definition_en: to tell people someone's name, to bring something in for the first time, or to begin something
core_image: 一个人牵着另一个人的手，把他领进一间坐满陌生人的屋子
scene: 晚宴开始时，主人走到客人身边，把他们两两凑在一起说名字。They introduced the new system last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 introduce 是「引进、推行」（第 2 个义项：把新事物带入使用），句意为他们去年春天引进了这套新系统。画面里的物件：晚宴长桌、香槟杯、贴着新标签的控制台。

pos.zh: 动词：介绍；引进；提出；作为……的开头

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -tion 构成，义为「介绍；引进；前言」
由本词加 -ory 构成，义为「引导性的；入门的」
由本词截短构成，义为「引言；开场」
同出 duc- 词根，义为「教育的」

senses.title: Make two people known
senses.definition: to tell two people each other's names so that they can begin to know each other
senses.definitionCN: 说出两人的名字，使他们可以开始相识
senses.example: Let me introduce my sister before we sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 坐下之前让我介绍一下我妹妹。
senses.why: Latin ducere means to lead; intro- means inward. To introduce is to lead someone in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ducere 意为「引导」，intro- 意为「向内」，introduce 就是把人领进来。

senses.title: Bring something in
senses.definition: to bring a new thing, idea, or rule into use for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 首次把新事物、新想法或新规定投入使用
senses.example: The school introduced a later start for older pupils.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为高年级学生推出了更晚的到校时间。
senses.why: The leading-in picture suits ideas too: new rules are walked into a system.
senses.whyCN: 「领进来」的图像也适用于想法：新规定被领进一个体系。

senses.title: Become familiar with
senses.definition: to cause someone to experience or learn about something for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 使某人第一次接触或了解某事物
senses.example: Her aunt introduced her to jazz when she was ten.
senses.exampleCN: 她十岁时，姑母带她第一次接触爵士乐。
senses.why: Here the person is led into a subject as if into a room.
senses.whyCN: 这里人是被领进一门学问，就像被领进一间屋子。

senses.title: Begin a piece
senses.definition: to begin a speech, book, or programme with something
senses.definitionCN: 用某内容作为演讲、书籍或节目的开头
senses.example: The chair introduced the meeting with two minutes of thanks.
senses.exampleCN: 主席用两分钟致谢作为会议的开场。
senses.why: Opening a meeting is leading the audience in, so the same verb serves.
senses.whyCN: 会议开场就是把听众领进来，所以还是用同一个动词。

intro.en: Introduce joins Latin intro- "inward" and ducere "to lead": to lead someone in.
intro.cn: introduce 把拉丁语 intro-「向内」与 ducere「引导」结合：把人领进来。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead or draw along.
items.cn: ducere 意为带领或牵引。

items.en: Introducere meant to lead a person or thing inside.
items.cn: introducere 意为把人或物领进去。

items.en: French introduire kept the ceremonial sense of bringing someone in.
items.cn: 法语 introduire 保留了把人带进来的礼仪义。

items.en: English used introduce for presenting a person at court or at home.
items.cn: 英语用 introduce 指在宫廷或家中引见某人。

items.en: Industry and law added the sense of putting a new thing into use.
items.cn: 工业与法律又添上「把新事物投入使用」义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -duce leading root; the near-meaning group holds other words for presenting.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -duce「引导」词根；近义组收其他表示「推出」的词。

entries.definition: The act or the opening section that results.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「介绍；引言」。

entries.definition: To lead something back or make it smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「减少」，同出 ducere。

entries.definition: To lead something forward into being.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「生产」，同出 ducere。

entries.definition: To show or hand over something formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「呈现；呈交」，更正式。

entries.definition: To start using something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语义为「引入」，偏口语。

entries.definition: To start a product or campaign publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「推出；发起」，强调公开。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a hand leading another person indoors.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「一只手把别人领进屋里」的画面。

normal.en: intro- inward plus duc lead equals lead in.
normal.cn: intro-「向内」加 duc「引导」等于「领进来」。

normal.en: The same duc root appears in reduce, produce, and conduct.
normal.cn: 同一个 duc 词根出现在 reduce、produce、conduct 里。

normal.en: Introduce yourself is the shortest formal speech you will give.
normal.cn: introduce yourself 是你要讲的最短的正式发言。

normal.en: Schools introduce rules the way hosts introduce guests.
normal.cn: 学校推行规定，就像主人介绍客人。

normal.en: Her aunt introduced her to jazz: led her into a room of sound.
normal.cn: 姑母带她认识爵士：把她领进一间装满声音的屋子。

abstract.en: To introduce is to open a door and stand aside.
abstract.cn: 介绍就是打开一扇门，然后退到一边。

abstract.en: New ideas also need someone to walk them in.
abstract.cn: 新想法也需要有人牵着走进去。

abstract.en: The word is a handshake turned into grammar.
abstract.cn: 这个词是把一次握手写成了语法。

examples.en: She introduced me to her old teacher at the gate.
examples.cn: 她在门口把我介绍给了她的老师。

examples.en: The company introduced a shorter working week.
examples.cn: 公司推行了更短的工作周。

examples.en: He introduced his talk with a story about his father.
examples.cn: 他用一个关于父亲的故事开了讲座的头。

dict_mnemonic.text: intro（向内）+ duce（引导）——把人领进门

root: 拉丁语 intro「向内」+ ducere「引导」→ introducere「领进去」→ 古法语 introduire → 英语 introduce。同族有 introduction、introductory、produce。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: make people known, bring something new in, lead someone into a subject, and open a piece.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：让人相识、引进新事物、带人入门，以及作为开场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand leading another person through a doorway.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手牵着另一个人穿过门口。

branches.en: THE NAMES: two strangers given to each other.
branches.cn: 名字这条线：两个陌生人被交给彼此。

branches.en: THE RULE: a new practice led into a system.
branches.cn: 规定这条线：新做法被领进一个体系。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a young listener led into jazz.
branches.cn: 唱片这条线：年轻听者被领进爵士。

branches.en: THE PODIUM: an opening line that leads the audience in.
branches.cn: 讲台这条线：把听众领进来的开场白。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses bring someone into a place they did not know.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都把某人带进他原本不认识的地方。

intro.en: Introduce is intro- "inward" plus the root duc- "lead" with the verb ending.
intro.cn: introduce 是 intro-「向内」加词根 duc-「引导」与动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere, introducere and the participle introductus are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ducere、introducere 与分词 introductus 均有记载。

items.example: It marks the direction of leading.
The root also appears in conduct and educate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 conduct 与 educate。

items.example: The verb is the base of the root.
The verb is the direct source.
It forms introduction.
It forms introductory.
It forms reduce, to lead back.
It forms produce, to lead forth.

definition_en: the act of making people known or bringing something in, or the opening part of a book or talk
core_image: 书的正文之前，有一页写着短短几段，把你领进门
scene: 新同事被带到办公区，组长领着他在每张桌前停下说一句。The book's introduction explains why the author began.
sceneCN: 这里 introduction 是「引言、前言」（第 4 个义项：书或讲话的开头部分），句意为这本书的引言说明了作者为何动笔。画面里的物件：新同事、工位、书的扉页。

pos.zh: 名词：介绍；引进；引言；入门介绍

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「介绍；引进」
由 introduce 加 -ory 构成，义为「引导性的」
截短形式，义为「开场；引言」

senses.title: Making people known
senses.definition: the act of telling two people each other's names so that they can meet
senses.definitionCN: 说出两人名字使他们得以相识的行为
senses.example: A quiet introduction at the door saved them both embarrassment.
senses.exampleCN: 门口一句轻轻的介绍替两人都免了尴尬。
senses.why: The Latin action noun treats the handshake as a deed with a name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语的动作名词把这次握手当成一件有名字的事。

senses.title: Bringing something in
senses.definition: the act of putting a new thing, rule, or idea into use
senses.definitionCN: 把新事物、规定或想法投入使用的行为
senses.example: The introduction of the railway changed the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路的引进改变了整个山谷。
senses.why: The same leading-in image applies to machines and policies.
senses.whyCN: 「领进来」的图像同样用于机器与政策。

senses.title: A first course
senses.definition: a book or course that teaches the basics of a subject
senses.definitionCN: 讲解某学科基础知识的一本书或一门课
senses.example: This little grammar is a gentle introduction to Latin.
senses.exampleCN: 这本薄薄的语法书是拉丁语的温和入门。
senses.why: A beginner is led in, so the teaching material takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 初学者是被领进去的，于是入门教材也叫这个名字。

senses.title: The opening part
senses.definition: the first section of a book, speech, or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 书籍、演讲或乐曲的最初部分
senses.example: Read the introduction before you judge the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 先读引言，再评判论证。
senses.why: The opening leads the reader in, exactly what the Latin verb described.
senses.whyCN: 开头把读者领进去，正是那个拉丁动词所描述的。

intro.en: Introduction is the Latin noun on introducere, to lead someone in.
intro.cn: introduction 是建立在 introducere（把人领进来）上的拉丁语名词。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead; intro- meant inward.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导」，intro- 意为「向内」。

items.en: Introductio named the act of bringing someone or something in.
items.cn: introductio 指把人或物带进来的行为。

items.en: French kept the noun for a formal presentation of persons.
items.cn: 法语保留了这个名词，指对人的正式引见。

items.en: Printing gave it the sense of the opening pages of a book.
items.cn: 印刷术给了它「书的开篇」义。

items.en: Modern usage adds the introduction of machines and reforms.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上机器与改革的引进。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -duct- leading stem; the near-meaning group holds other opening words.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -duct-「引导」词干；近义组收其他「开头」词。

entries.definition: The verb of leading someone in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「介绍；引进」。

entries.definition: The adjective for an opening section.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「引导性的」。

entries.definition: The making of goods or a show.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「生产；制作」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A short note before the main text.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「序言」，作者自述写作缘由。

entries.definition: An opening note often written by someone else.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「前言」，多由他人撰写。

entries.definition: A general summary before the details.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「概述」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks treat the word as the doorway into a book or a group.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它当作一本书或一群人的门口。

normal.en: Introduce is the act; introduction is the act turned into a thing.
normal.cn: introduce 是动作，introduction 是被做成东西的动作。

normal.en: An introduction to economics leads you into the subject.
normal.cn: an introduction to economics 把你领进这门学科。

normal.en: Letters of introduction once opened doors in a new city.
normal.cn: 介绍信曾在陌生城市替你开门。

normal.en: The introduction of the railway is the same word used for machines.
normal.cn: the introduction of the railway 是同词用于机器。

normal.en: Skip the introduction and you may miss why the book exists.
normal.cn: 跳过引言可能就错过了这本书存在的理由。

abstract.en: An introduction is a corridor, not a room.
abstract.cn: 引言是走廊，不是房间。

abstract.en: Every introduction asks you to trust before you know.
abstract.cn: 每次介绍都在你了解之前先请你信任。

abstract.en: A good introduction hands you a lamp, not a map.
abstract.cn: 好的引言递给你一盏灯，而不是一张地图。

examples.en: His introduction to her was made by a mutual friend.
examples.cn: 他是通过一位共同的朋友认识她的。

examples.en: The introduction of parking fees angered local shops.
examples.cn: 停车费的引入让本地商铺不满。

examples.en: She wrote a short introduction to the second edition.
examples.cn: 她为第二版写了一篇简短的引言。

dict_mnemonic.text: intro（向内）+ duct（引导）+ ion——把人领进来的那段

root: 拉丁语 intro「向内」+ ducere「引导」→ introductio「引见」→ 古法语 → 英语 introduction。同族有 introduce、introductory、intro。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: making people known, bringing something new in, a beginner's course, and an opening section.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：让人相识、引进新事物、入门课程，以及开篇部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few short pages standing before the main text like a doorman.
core.cn: 核心意象：正文之前几页短文，像一个门房站在那里。

branches.en: THE HANDSHAKE: two people given each other's names.
branches.cn: 握手这条线：两个人被互相报出名字。

branches.en: THE RAILWAY: a new thing led into daily life.
branches.cn: 铁路这条线：新事物被领进日常生活。

branches.en: THE TEXTBOOK: a gentle first course.
branches.cn: 课本这条线：温和的第一课。

branches.en: THE PREFACE: the opening that explains the whole.
branches.cn: 序言这条线：解释全书的开头。

branches.en: THE LINK: both stand at a door and say what comes next.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都站在门口，说明接下来是什么。

intro.en: Introduction is intro- plus the root duct- "lead" and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: introduction 由 intro- 加词根 duct-「引导」与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin introductio and the participle introductus are recorded forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 introductio 与分词 introductus 都是记载形式。

items.example: It marks the direction of entry.
The root also appears in conduct and product.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 conduct 与 product。

items.example: The noun is the direct source.
It builds the abstract noun.
The verb is the base of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的基础。

items.example: It forms introductory.
It builds preface, said beforehand.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 preface，意为先说在前。

items.example: It builds foreword, the word in front.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 foreword，即前面的文字。

definition_zh: 投资；投入（时间精力）；授予（权力）
definition_en: to put money, time, or effort into something hoping for a return, or to formally give someone power or a right
core_image: 一笔钱被装进土里，等着日后长出更多
scene: 父亲把存折推到女儿面前，让她自己决定怎么用这笔学费之外的钱。She decided to invest half of it in a small bakery.
sceneCN: 这里 invest 是「投资」（第 1 个义项：把钱投出去以求回报），句意为她决定把其中一半投进一家小面包店。画面里的物件：存折、桌面、台灯。

pos.zh: 动词：投资；投入；授予权力

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「投资；投资额」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「投资者」
加前缀 di- 构成的反向词，义为「撤资；剥夺」
去掉 in- 的同源词，义为「背心；授予」

senses.title: Putting money to work
senses.definition: to put money into a business or asset in order to make a profit later
senses.definitionCN: 把钱放进企业或资产，指望日后获利
senses.example: They invested their savings in solar panels for the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把积蓄投在了屋顶的太阳能板上。
senses.why: Latin investire meant "to clothe", and money clothed in a venture was said to be invested.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investire 意为「给穿衣」，钱被「穿」进一桩事业，就叫投了出去。

senses.title: Spending effort
senses.definition: to give time, energy, or attention to something because it matters
senses.definitionCN: 因为某事重要而付出时间、精力或注意力
senses.example: She invested three years in learning the violin.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了三年时间学小提琴。
senses.why: If money can be dressed in a project, so can effort: both are resources you part with.
senses.whyCN: 钱能披挂在一个项目上，力气也行：两者都是你交出去的资源。

senses.title: Giving formal power
senses.definition: to give someone the official right or power to act in a role
senses.definitionCN: 正式赋予某人在某职位上行动的权力
senses.example: The new mayor was invested with the authority to hire staff.
senses.exampleCN: 新市长被授予聘用员工的权力。
senses.why: The oldest sense is ceremonial: a robe was put on someone to show the office was now theirs.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是仪式性的：给别人穿上礼服，表示职位从此归他。

intro.en: Invest began as a word about clothes and ceremony long before it meant money.
intro.cn: invest 在表示钱之前，长期是个关于衣服与仪式的词。

items.en: The noun vestis meant "garment".
items.cn: 名词 vestis 意为「衣服」。

items.en: investire meant "to put a garment on someone".
items.cn: investire 意为「给人穿上衣服」。

items.en: The Church used it for dressing a person in the robes of an office.
items.cn: 教会用它表示给人穿上某职位的礼服。

items.en: Trade turned the idea of clothing into placing money in a venture.
items.cn: 商业把「穿衣」的想法转成了把钱放进一桩事业。

items.en: Banks and markets fixed the financial sense in everyday speech.
items.cn: 银行与市场把这一金融义固定进了日常语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vest- stem; the near-meaning group holds words about putting resources in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vest- 词干；近义组收表示投入资源的词。

entries.definition: A sleeveless garment worn under a jacket.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「背心」，同词根。

entries.definition: To sell off holdings or strip someone of power.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「撤资；剥夺」，反向词。

entries.definition: To create something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「发明」，拼写只差一个字母。

entries.definition: To provide money for a project.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「资助」，提供资金。

entries.definition: To give time or attention completely to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「奉献」，强调全心全意。

entries.definition: To set money or resources aside for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「拨出」，指分配。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move the word from a robe to a wallet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个词从礼服挪到钱包。

normal.en: in- means in, and vest- means clothes.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vest- 是「衣服」。

normal.en: Money is dressed in a project, so it is invested.
normal.cn: 钱被「穿」在项目上，所以叫投进去。

normal.en: What you put in is an investment.
normal.cn: 你放进去的那笔就叫 investment。

normal.en: The person who puts it in is an investor.
normal.cn: 放进去的人叫 investor。

normal.en: Dress effort in a cause and you invest in it too.
normal.cn: 把力气披挂在一件事上，也是 invest。

abstract.en: Investment is trust wearing a price tag.
abstract.cn: 投资是贴上价签的信任。

abstract.en: To invest is to plant and then leave the field alone.
abstract.cn: 投资是种下去，然后先别去动那块地。

abstract.en: Power, like money, is handed over by an act of dressing.
abstract.cn: 权力和钱一样，都靠一个「加衣」的动作交出去。

examples.en: The fund invests mainly in small farms.
examples.cn: 这只基金主要投资小型农场。

examples.en: He invested every spare hour in the repair of the boat.
examples.cn: 他把每一个空闲小时都投在了修船上。

examples.en: The board invested the director with full control of the budget.
examples.cn: 董事会授予这位主管完全的预算控制权。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vest（衣服）——把钱裹进项目里

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vestis「衣服」→ investire「给穿衣」→ 中世纪拉丁语指授职 → 英语 invest 引申为「投资」。同族有 investment、investor、divest、vest。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: putting in money, putting in effort, and formally granting power.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：投入金钱、投入精力，以及正式授予权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something valuable is handed over and dressed in a new role.
core.cn: 核心意象：有价值的东西被交出去，并披上一个新的身份。

branches.en: THE PURSE: money placed where it can grow.
branches.cn: 钱包这条线：放在能生长之处的钱。

branches.en: THE HOURS: time given to a craft or cause.
branches.cn: 时间这条线：给一门手艺或一件事的时间。

branches.en: THE ROBE: official authority put on a person.
branches.cn: 礼服这条线：披在某人身上的官方权力。

branches.en: THE RESOURCE: both senses part with something now for later.
branches.cn: 资源这条线：两个义项都是现在付出、以后收获。

branches.en: THE GRANT: both senses make a formal transfer of value.
branches.cn: 授予这条线：两个义项都完成一次正式的价值转移。

intro.en: Invest is in- "into" plus vestis "garment"; the robe may be worn by a man or by money.
intro.cn: invest 是 in-「进入」加 vestis「衣服」，穿上礼服的可能是人，也可能是钱。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestis, vestire and investire are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestis、vestire 与 investire 均有记载。

items.example: It puts the garment on.
The root names what is put on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被穿上的东西。

items.example: It forms investment.
It forms investor.
The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.example: The bare stem still names a piece of clothing.
items.exampleCN: 光词干至今仍指一件衣服。

items.example: It builds divest, to strip away.
The prefix reverses the direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把方向反了过来。

definition_en: to examine a situation, event, or person carefully in order to find out the truth
core_image: 一只手举着灯，在地上一点点照着找脚印
scene: 雨后的院子里，两个人蹲下来，用手电照着泥地，看脚印往哪个方向走。Police are investigating the cause of the fire.
sceneCN: 这里 investigate 是「调查」（第 1 个义项：为查明真相而仔细查），句意为警方正在调查火灾的起因。画面里的物件：手电、泥地脚印、警戒线。

pos.zh: 动词：调查；研究；侦察

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「调查」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「调查员」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「调查性的」
同源词，义为「痕迹」

senses.title: Look into a case
senses.definition: to try to find out the facts about a crime, accident, or complaint
senses.definitionCN: 设法查清犯罪、事故或投诉的事实
senses.example: Officers are investigating the break-in at the school.
senses.exampleCN: 警员正在调查学校那次闯入事件。
senses.why: Latin vestigium means a footprint, and the verb meant to follow footprints.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vestigium 意为「脚印」，那个动词意为「循脚印追查」。

senses.title: Study to understand
senses.definition: to examine something systematically in order to understand how it works
senses.definitionCN: 为理解其运作方式而系统地检视某事物
senses.example: Scientists are investigating why the lake is warming.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家正在研究这座湖为何变暖。
senses.why: The same footprint-following works for nature as for crime.
senses.whyCN: 循脚印追查既用于案件，也用于自然现象。

senses.title: Examine a person
senses.definition: to question or examine a person officially to judge their part in something
senses.definitionCN: 为判断某人在事件中的角色而正式讯问或审查
senses.example: Two managers were investigated over the payments.
senses.exampleCN: 两名经理因这些款项受到调查。
senses.why: People also leave tracks, so the verb turns from things to persons.
senses.whyCN: 人也会留下痕迹，于是这个动词从物转向人。

senses.title: Explore a possibility
senses.definition: to look into whether something is possible or true before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在决定之前先弄清某事是否可能或属实
senses.example: We should investigate whether the hall can hold two hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 我们该查一查礼堂能不能容纳两百人。
senses.why: The cautious sense checks facts before a decision is made.
senses.whyCN: 这种谨慎用法是在决定之前先核实。

intro.en: Investigate comes from Latin investigare, to follow footprints, from vestigium, a footprint.
intro.cn: investigate 来自拉丁语 investigare「循脚印追查」，源出 vestigium「脚印」。

items.en: Vestigium meant a footprint or a trace left behind.
items.cn: vestigium 意为脚印或留下的痕迹。

items.en: Investigare meant to track something by its traces.
items.cn: investigare 意为顺着痕迹追踪。

items.en: The noun investigatio named the tracing itself.
items.cn: 名词 investigatio 指这番追踪。

items.en: English used investigate for legal and scholarly inquiry.
items.cn: 英语用 investigate 指法律与学术的查究。

items.en: Police work made it a familiar verb of daily news.
items.cn: 警务让它成为新闻里的常用动词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the invest- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for inquiry.
note.cn: 形近组共用 invest- 开头；近义组收表示查究的词。

entries.definition: The inquiry itself as a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「调查」。

entries.definition: To put money into something for a return.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「投资」，拼写近似。

entries.definition: A small remaining trace of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「残留的痕迹」，同出 vestigium。

entries.definition: To look at something closely and carefully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「检查」，偏细看。

entries.definition: To search into something awkward or hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「探究」，语气更锐利。

entries.definition: To try to find out about something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语义为「查一查」，偏口语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the footprint at the heart of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用这个词心里的那只脚印。

normal.en: Vestigium means footprint; to investigate is to follow the prints.
normal.cn: vestigium 意为脚印；investigate 就是顺着脚印走。

normal.en: The same trace survives in vestige, a leftover mark.
normal.cn: 同样的痕迹留在 vestige 里，那是残余的印记。

normal.en: Police investigate crimes; scientists investigate causes.
normal.cn: 警察调查案件，科学家研究成因。

normal.en: Under investigation means the prints are still warm.
normal.cn: under investigation 意思是脚印还没凉。

normal.en: Do not mix it with invest, which is about money.
normal.cn: 别和 invest 混：那个词讲的是钱。

abstract.en: Investigation is patience with a lamp.
abstract.cn: 调查是举着灯的一点耐心。

abstract.en: Every fact leaves a print somewhere.
abstract.cn: 每个事实都会在某处留下印子。

abstract.en: To investigate is to admit you do not yet know.
abstract.cn: 调查等于承认自己还不知道。

examples.en: The committee will investigate how the money was spent.
examples.cn: 委员会将调查这笔钱是如何花掉的。

examples.en: She investigated the strange noise in the attic.
examples.cn: 她去查了阁楼里那奇怪的声音。

examples.en: He was investigated twice and cleared both times.
examples.cn: 他两次受到调查，两次都洗清了。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vestige（痕迹）+ ate——顺着痕迹查进去

root: 拉丁语 vestigium「脚印」→ investigare「循迹追查」→ 英语 investigate。同族有 investigation、investigator、vestige。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: look into a case, study how something works, examine a person, and test a possibility.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：查案、研究运作原理、审查某人，以及核实某种可能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp on the ground, following prints through mud.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏照在地上的灯，顺着泥里的脚印走。

branches.en: THE CASE: officers tracing what happened.
branches.cn: 案件这条线：警员追查发生了什么。

branches.en: THE LAKE: researchers tracing why it warms.
branches.cn: 湖这条线：研究者追查变暖的原因。

branches.en: THE MANAGER: a person questioned about payments.
branches.cn: 经理这条线：就款项受到询问的人。

branches.en: THE HALL: checking a fact before deciding.
branches.cn: 礼堂这条线：决定之前先核实。

branches.en: THE LINK: both follow traces towards a hidden cause.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都顺着痕迹追向隐藏的原因。

intro.en: Investigate is in- "in" plus the Latin stem vestig- "trace" and a verb ending.
intro.cn: investigate 是 in-「在内」加拉丁词干 vestig-「痕迹」与动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestigium, investigare and investigatio are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium、investigare 与 investigatio 均有记载。

items.example: It marks following into a trail.
The stem also appears in vestige.
The noun gives the whole picture.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词给了整幅画面。

items.example: The verb is the direct source.
It marks the English verb.
It forms investigation.
It forms investigator.
It forms investigative.

definition_en: a careful, formal attempt to find out the facts about an event, problem, or claim
core_image: 手电照着地面，一步步顺着脚印往里查
scene: 办公室里文件摊满桌面，两个人对着账本逐页核对日期。The investigation found that two payments had been recorded twice.
sceneCN: 这里 investigation 是「调查」（第 1 个义项：为弄清事实而做的正式查证），句意为调查发现有两笔付款被记了两次。画面里的物件：账本、桌面、荧光笔。

pos.zh: 名词：调查；侦查；研究

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 换 -ate，义为「调查；侦查」
由 investigate 加 -or 构成，义为「调查员」
由 investigate 词干加 -ive 构成，义为「调查性的」

senses.title: Official fact-finding
senses.definition: a formal process in which an authority examines evidence to establish the truth
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构审查证据、确定真相的正式过程
senses.example: A government investigation cleared the factory of any fault.
senses.exampleCN: 政府调查澄清这家工厂没有过错。
senses.why: Latin investigare meant "to follow the footprints", from in- plus vestigium, "track".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investigare 意为「跟着脚印走」，由 in- 加 vestigium「足迹」构成。

senses.title: Police or detective work
senses.definition: the work of police or detectives gathering facts about a suspected crime
senses.definitionCN: 警方或侦探就疑似犯罪收集事实的工作
senses.example: The investigation into the missing paintings lasted four years.
senses.exampleCN: 对失踪画作的侦查持续了四年。
senses.why: The footprint image fits best here: a detective literally follows a trail.
senses.whyCN: 「脚印」这个意象在这里最贴切：侦探就是顺着痕迹走的人。

senses.title: Careful study of a problem
senses.definition: a thorough academic or scientific study of a question
senses.definitionCN: 对某个问题所作的详尽学术或科学研究
senses.example: Her investigation of soil bacteria changed the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她对土壤细菌的研究改变了这个领域。
senses.why: Science borrowed the word because a good study also follows traces until a pattern shows.
senses.whyCN: 科学借用了这个词，因为好的研究同样顺着痕迹走到规律显现。

intro.en: Investigation carries a picture of footprints: Latin vestigium means "track".
intro.cn: investigation 带着脚印的画面：拉丁语 vestigium 意为「足迹」。

items.en: vestigium meant "footprint, trace".
items.cn: vestigium 意为「脚印、痕迹」。

items.en: investigare meant "to follow a track".
items.cn: investigare 意为「跟着足迹走」。

items.en: The noun investigatio named the search itself.
items.cn: 名词 investigatio 指这场追寻。

items.en: English took the noun for legal and official enquiries.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词用于法律与官方查问。

items.en: Science adopted it for systematic study as well.
items.cn: 科学界也采用它表示系统性研究。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vestigi- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for searching out facts.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vestigi- 词干；近义组收表示查明事实的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to look into a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「调查」，同词干。

entries.definition: Money put in for a return.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投资」，开头相同。

entries.definition: A request to come somewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「邀请」，尾音相近。

entries.definition: A question or a formal look into facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「询问；查问」。

entries.definition: A close and often official examination.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「探查」，常指官方深入检查。

entries.definition: Systematic study to discover new facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「研究」，偏学术。

normalIntro.en: These hooks all walk along a set of footprints.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都沿着同一串脚印走。

normal.en: in- means into, and vestigium means footprint.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vestigium 是「脚印」。

normal.en: To investigate is to follow the prints in.
normal.cn: investigate 就是顺着脚印往里查。

normal.en: The noun investigation is the whole walk.
normal.cn: 名词 investigation 指这整段路。

normal.en: An investigator is the one holding the torch.
normal.cn: investigator 是那个举着手电的人。

normal.en: Under investigation means the trail is still warm.
normal.cn: under investigation 意思是痕迹还热着。

abstract.en: Investigation is doubt that refuses to stay lazy.
abstract.cn: 调查是不肯偷懒的怀疑。

abstract.en: Every fact leaves a footprint; the word is the act of bending down.
abstract.cn: 每个事实都留下脚印；这个词就是弯腰去看。

abstract.en: A careful inquiry turns noise into a line.
abstract.cn: 仔细的查证把杂音拉成一条线。

examples.en: The investigation into the fire took almost a year.
examples.cn: 对那场火灾的调查花了将近一年。

examples.en: Two officers were suspended while under investigation.
examples.cn: 两名警员在接受调查期间被停职。

examples.en: Her investigation of the lake water found traces of lead.
examples.cn: 她对湖水的调查发现了微量的铅。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vestig（脚印）+ ation（名词）——顺着脚印查到底

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vestigium「足迹」→ investigare「跟踪追查」→ investigatio → 英语 investigation。同族有 investigate、investigator、investigative。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: an official inquiry, police detective work, and a thorough study of a question.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：官方查证、警方侦查，以及对某个问题的深入研究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: following a trail of footprints until the truth shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：顺着脚印走，直到真相显现。

branches.en: THE FILE: officials checking records against facts.
branches.cn: 档案这条线：官员把记录与事实对照。

branches.en: THE TRAIL: detectives walking a case to its end.
branches.cn: 痕迹这条线：侦探把一个案子走到底。

branches.en: THE LAB: researchers chasing a pattern through data.
branches.cn: 实验室这条线：研究者在数据里追一个规律。

branches.en: THE PROOF: both senses need evidence that holds up.
branches.cn: 证据这条线：两个义项都要站得住的证据。

branches.en: THE METHOD: both senses proceed step by step.
branches.cn: 方法这条线：两个义项都一步一步推进。

intro.en: Investigation is in- "into", vestigium "track", -ate the verb ending, and -ion for the act.
intro.cn: investigation 由 in-「进入」、vestigium「足迹」、动词尾 -ate 与名词尾 -ion 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestigium and investigare are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium 与 investigare 均有记载。

items.example: It marks walking inward along a trace.
The root is the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是这个词的心脏。

items.example: It forms the verb investigate.
It forms investigation.
It forms investigator.
It forms investigative.
The verb is the direct source.
The bare root still names a trace left behind.
items.exampleCN: 光词根仍指留下的痕迹。

definition_zh: 投资；投资额；投入；投资物
definition_en: money put into something in order to gain a profit or benefit, or the act of putting it there
core_image: 一叠钱被放进一个还在长的树坑里，等着以后长出来
scene: 老人把攒下的钱投进一家小工厂，又花两年时间教工人手艺。The new road was a huge public investment.
sceneCN: 这里 investment 是「投资」（第 1 个义项：为获利而投入的钱或投入行为），句意为新道路是一项巨大的公共投资。画面里的物件：存折、树坑、工厂图纸。

pos.zh: 名词：投资；投资额；投入；投资物

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「投资」
由 invest 加 -or 构成，义为「投资者」
由 invest 加 -ing 构成，义为「投资行为」
同源词，义为「授职仪式」

senses.title: Money put in for gain
senses.definition: money placed in a business, property, or scheme in the hope of earning more
senses.definitionCN: 为求得更多回报而投入企业、房产或项目的钱
senses.example: She made a small investment in a friend's bakery.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家朋友的烘焙店做了小额投资。
senses.why: Latin investire meant to clothe; the money is dressed in a new form, hoping to grow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investire 意为「给……穿衣」，钱换了件衣裳，指望长大。

senses.title: The act of putting in
senses.definition: the act or process of putting money or effort into something
senses.definitionCN: 把钱或精力投入某事的行为或过程
senses.example: Investment in new machines rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年对新机器的投资大幅上升。
senses.why: The noun can name the deed rather than the sum.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以指动作，而不指金额。

senses.title: Time or effort given
senses.definition: time, energy, or care given to something in the belief that it will pay off
senses.definitionCN: 相信会有回报而在某事上给出的时间、精力或关心
senses.example: Learning the language was an investment of three years.
senses.exampleCN: 学这门语言是三年的投入。
senses.why: Despite the money picture, the word readily counts hours as well as cash.
senses.whyCN: 尽管有金钱的画面，这个词同样能算小时，不限于现金。

senses.title: A thing invested in
senses.definition: a business, property, or asset in which money has been placed
senses.definitionCN: 已经投入资金的生意、房产或资产
senses.example: Their investments are mostly in land near the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的投资大多在城市近郊的土地上。
senses.why: By transfer the noun moves from the act to the holdings themselves.
senses.whyCN: 经转喻，名词从行为转到所持有的资产上。

intro.en: Investment comes from Latin investire, to clothe, through the idea of money put into a new dress.
intro.cn: investment 来自拉丁语 investire「给……穿衣」，经由「把钱换上新衣」的想法而来。

items.en: Vestire meant to clothe; in- meant into.
items.cn: vestire 意为穿衣，in- 意为进入。

items.en: Investire meant to dress someone in a robe of office.
items.cn: investire 意为给某人穿上就职礼袍。

items.en: English used invest for giving power or a rank.
items.cn: 英语用 invest 指授予权力或职位。

items.en: Commerce added the sense of dressing money in a venture.
items.cn: 商业又添上「把钱打扮成一项生意」义。

items.en: Investment then named the sum, the act, and the assets.
items.cn: investment 由此兼指金额、行为与资产。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the invest- stem; the near-meaning group holds money words.
note.cn: 形近组共用 invest- 词干；近义组收金融相关的词。

entries.definition: The verb of putting money in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「投资」。

entries.definition: The person who puts money in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「投资者」。

entries.definition: To examine in order to find the truth.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「调查」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: Money provided for a project.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「资金」，多指拨款。

entries.definition: Money used to start or grow a business.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「资本」。

entries.definition: Money placed in a bank account.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「存款」，偏储蓄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks hold on to the image of money dressed up to grow.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子抓住「钱换上衣裳去长大」的画面。

normal.en: Invest originally meant to clothe; investment dresses money in a venture.
normal.cn: invest 本义是穿衣；investment 给钱换上生意的衣裳。

normal.en: Return on investment asks whether the new clothes paid off.
normal.cn: return on investment 问的就是这身新衣有没有回本。

normal.en: You can invest money, time, or patience.
normal.cn: 钱、时间、耐心都可以 invest。

normal.en: Foreign investment moves across borders looking for growth.
normal.cn: foreign investment 越过边界寻找增长。

normal.en: Keep it apart from investigate, which follows footprints.
normal.cn: 别和 investigate 混：那个词是顺着脚印查。

abstract.en: Investment is a promise made in the form of money.
abstract.cn: 投资是用钱的形式做出的一句承诺。

abstract.en: Every tree you water is an investment in shade.
abstract.cn: 你浇的每一棵树，都是对荫凉做的投资。

abstract.en: Time is the only investment that cannot be recovered.
abstract.cn: 时间是唯一不可收回的投资。

examples.en: The factory needs foreign investment to expand.
examples.cn: 这家工厂需要外国投资才能扩张。

examples.en: Her years of study were an investment in herself.
examples.cn: 多年的学习是她对自己的投资。

examples.en: He sold his investments before the market fell.
examples.cn: 市场下跌前他卖掉了手上的投资。

dict_mnemonic.text: invest（投入）+ ment（名词）——投进去的那笔东西

root: 拉丁语 vestire「穿衣」→ investire「穿上官袍、授予」→ 英语 invest（投资），加 -ment 成 investment。同族有 invest、investor、investigate。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: money put in for gain, the act of putting in, effort given, and the assets held.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：为获利投入的钱、投入行为、付出的心力，以及所持有的资产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of money planted in a pit like a seed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠钱像种子一样被埋进土坑。

branches.en: THE BAKERY: a small sum placed in a friend's shop.
branches.cn: 烘焙店这条线：投进朋友店里的小笔钱。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: spending turned into a process.
branches.cn: 机器这条线：被当作过程来看的支出。

branches.en: THE LANGUAGE: three years paid into a skill.
branches.cn: 语言这条线：为一项技能付出的三年。

branches.en: THE LAND: the holdings the money now lives in.
branches.cn: 土地这条线：钱如今栖身的那些资产。

branches.en: THE LINK: both trust that today's cost becomes tomorrow's gain.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都相信今天的代价会换来明天的收获。

intro.en: Investment is invest plus the noun ending -ment, from Latin vestire "to clothe".
intro.cn: investment 是 invest 加名词词尾 -ment，源自拉丁语 vestire「穿衣」。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestire and investire are recorded; the money sense is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestire 与 investire 有记载，而「投资」义是英语后来添的。

items.example: It marks putting something into something.
items.exampleCN: 它标出把一物放进另一物。

items.example: The root also appears in vestment.
The verb is the direct source.
It builds the English noun.
It forms investor.
It forms investing.
It keeps the oldest sense.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了最古老的意思。

items.meaning: what comes back to the investor
items.example: It names the gain hoped for.
